candidate_relations.reason: Normal ANCA and inflammatory markers plus repeated AFB PCR positivity favor mycobacterial infection over granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
Symptoms began in later adulthood and no lifelong pulmonary or otologic phenotype suggests primary ciliary dyskinesia.
Pseudomonas grew from the destructive sinus cavity, but noncaseating granulomas and positive AFB PCR indicate an additional acid-fast process underlying the reference diagnosis.
HIV testing is negative and the record gives no immune defect despite the unusual chronic infection.
Five years of crusting, purulence, and sinus destruction establish chronic rhinosinusitis, but the term omits the acid-fast organism and granulomatous etiology.
AFB PCR is positive, yet the record reports no caseating granulomas, constitutional symptoms, or species result establishing Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
The destructive nasal process could mimic rhinoscleroma, but positive AFB probes and no Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis result support another organism.
Noncaseating granulomas are documented in sinus mucosa, although an unspecified granulomatous label loses the infectious sinus site and mycobacterial identity.

case_quality_flags: The record reports positive AFB PCR but no species-level assay or culture naming Mycobacterium chelonae.
